validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: solidly confirmed independent of GEM. Enbridge's own current asset factsheet (FS_EnergyInfrastructureAssets.pdf, downloaded and read with pdftotext) devotes a full page to 'Algonquin Gas Transmission' describing a 1,131-mile, 3.09 Bcf/d interstate line through NJ/NY/CT/RI/MA. offshore-technology.com's marketdata page independently states the same 1,820 km length and a 1953 start. Wikipedia (stub article, 'Algonquin Gas Transmission Pipeline') independently confirms Enbridge ownership and the New England service area. The wiki's harvested citation pool additionally contains ~15 mainstream news articles (NYT, WBUR, Commonwealth Magazine, Boston Business Journal, WAMC, lohud, Concord Monitor, Kallanish, RTO Insider) covering the 2014-2017 AIM expansion and the Weymouth compressor controversy — all describing a real, physically-built, FERC-regulated interstate pipeline, not a paper project. CLASSIFICATION: transmission/gas is correct — every source describes an interstate natural gas transmission trunkline, never a gathering or NGL line. DUPLICATE CHECK vs roster: P0150 'Algonquin Incremental Market (AIM)' (37 mi, 42 in, cap 342) is NOT the same physical scope as this row. The Enbridge factsheet's ownership breakdown lists two separate membership interests for the same overall system — '100% Algonquin Base Business' (matches P0149, Enbridge 100%) vs '85% Algonquin Incremental Market project' + '15% Eversource Energy' (a materially different ownership structure, matching a discrete FERC-authorized expansion project, i.e. P0150) — confirming GEM's Main-Line/AIM split is a real distinction the operator itself makes, not a duplicate/double-count. Of the 37 harvested wiki citations I opened/tested: the Enbridge factsheet (opened+read in full), offshore-technology.com (opened), the EIA data.php portal (already an existing sheet ref, previously checked), and two old citation URLs that are now dead (FERC 'CalendarFiles' PDF from 2015 -> 404 on ferc.gov's current site; the PHMSA primis.phmsa.dot.gov operator-report URL from 2017 -> redirects to a generic PHMSA enforcement landing page, no operator content). I did not individually open the remaining ~15 opposition/political-coverage articles (Indian Point protest coverage, the cancelled 'Access Northeast' project, MoveOn/SAPE activist pages) since by their headlines/context they concern the AIM expansion controversy or a separate cancelled project, not P0149 Main Line's own specs — flagged here for the record rather than silently skipped.

validity.recommendation: Correct StartState/Province from 'New York' to 'New Jersey'. Lambertville (the recorded StartLocation) is a New Jersey borough on the Delaware River, not a New York location, and Enbridge's own factsheet names the states in route order as 'New Jersey, New York, Connecticut, Rhode Island and Massachusetts' — New Jersey first, matching a Lambertville, NJ origin at the Texas Eastern interconnect.
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet has StartLocation=Lambertville / StartState/Province=New York. There is no Lambertville, NY that I could find; Lambertville, NJ (Hunterdon County) is the well-known town at this name, sitting across the Delaware River from New Hope, PA, and is a documented Texas Eastern/Algonquin interconnect point. The Enbridge factsheet (own-operator source, quote: 'The Algonquin Gas Transmission pipeline transports 3.09 Bcf/d of natural gas through 1,131 miles of pipeline through New Jersey, New York, Connecticut, Rhode Island and Massachusetts') lists New Jersey as the first state, consistent with a Lambertville, NJ start and New York being a pass-through state, not the origin. I looked for a second independent source to corroborate NJ specifically (Wikipedia's Algonquin article is a stub with no route/state detail at all; the wiki-cited FERC CP14-96 PDF and PHMSA operator-report URLs are both dead links now; DuckDuckGo/Bing scraping returned no usable plain-text snippets in this environment, and this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before I could try further queries). Flagging at medium tier on one strong, directly-on-point primary (operator) source rather than silently accepting the current value or fabricating a second citation.

validity.recommendation: Re-verify StartYear1. The existing 'Start [ref]' (EIA data.php) does not actually contain '1997' per the worklist's own pre-check, and independent evidence says the mainline entered service in 1953 — the same year as the sheet's own (unreferenced) ConstructionYear. A pipeline commissioned in 1953 having no recorded start-of-service until 1997 (a 44-year gap) is internally inconsistent; 1953 is the better-supported candidate pending a primary source that actually explains what 1997 refers to (possibly a specific expansion phase mis-mapped onto StartYear1).
validity.researcher_notes: offshore-technology.com states plainly that 'The Algonquin Gas project started operations in 1953' — the same source (and figure) that supports ConstructionYear. That leaves no independent support anywhere I checked for '1997' as an in-service year: the current Start [ref] (https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php#pipelines) is a generic portal page, and the worklist's own existing_ref_checks entry for this unit already flags '200 but data value not found (none of ["1997","1,997"])'. I could not identify what 1997 event this might correctly describe (no FERC docket, news article, or factsheet in the pool mentions a 1997 Algonquin expansion or in-service milestone) — it may be a transcription/confusion with a different expansion year (e.g., the 1990s-era 'Stony Point' or a HubLine-adjacent project) that was never disambiguated when originally staged. Recommend a targeted FERC eLibrary search for Algonquin Gas Transmission Co. dockets from the mid-1990s before overwriting; I'm not confident enough to just paste 1953 in without that check, hence tier=low.

validity.recommendation: Verify the exact current peak-day design capacity before citing a ref for the sheet's 3,120 MMcf/d. Enbridge's own factsheet — the most authoritative source found — states 'peak day capacity: 3.09 Bcf/d' (3,090 MMcf/d), about 1% below the sheet value. The two numbers are close but do not match exactly, and I found no source stating 3,120 specifically.
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet: Capacity=3120.00 MMcf/d, no ref (MISSING_REF). Enbridge factsheet (current, ~2021 vintage, opened and read via pdftotext): 'peak day capacity: 3.09 Bcf/d' = 3,090 MMcf/d for the same 1,131-mile system — this is the strongest source available (the pipeline's own operator) but is a single source and is ~1% off the sheet's figure, so I'm flagging rather than silently confirming 3,120. Separately, Wikipedia's stub article gives capacity as 'about 20 billion cubic meters (bcm) of natural gas per annum' (≈ 1,933 MMcf/d) — I checked this and it disagrees with both the sheet and the Enbridge factsheet by roughly 35-38%; given Wikipedia's article is thin/unmaintained and Algonquin has gone through multiple capacity-adding expansions since (AIM ~2017 alone added ~342 MMcf/d, per P0150, plus Atlantic Bridge), I believe the Wikipedia figure is stale/pre-expansion and should not be used to corroborate either 3,090 or 3,120 — noting it here only so a reviewer doesn't independently rediscover and get confused by the same discrepancy. Recommend confirming the precise current figure via a FERC tariff Index of Customers/Statement of Operating Conditions or a dated Enbridge/Spectra 10-K before pasting either 3,090 or 3,120 with a ref.

cross_row_leads.facts: The Enbridge factsheet's ownership line for the whole Algonquin system reads: 'Ownership: Enbridge (100% Algonquin Base Business membership interest and 85% Algonquin Incremental Market project membership interest); Eversource Energy (15% Algonquin Incremental Market project membership interest).' P0150 is GEM's row for the Algonquin Incremental Market (AIM) project — its Owner column should likely show Enbridge 85% / Eversource Energy 15%, not just Enbridge 100%. Worth checking P0150's current Owner values against this.

This is the FERC docket the GEM wiki page cites for the AIM project (Docket No. CP14-96-000, March 3, 2015), but the URL is now dead (404 on the current ferc.gov site structure — old CalendarFiles path was retired). Worth a Wayback-machine or eLibrary re-fetch when researching P0150, since this is likely the certificate order stating AIM's added capacity/length/diameter.

summary: P0149 (Algonquin Gas Transmission Main Line): existence/classification/duplicate-identity all confirmed (Enbridge factsheet + offshore-technology + extensive trade press; correctly distinct from P0150/AIM) — but 4 spec/attribution concerns staged: StartState/Province wrong (New York -> should be New Jersey per Lambertville + Enbridge's own state list), StartYear1=1997 unsupported/likely wrong (should probably be 1953, matching ConstructionYear), Capacity=3120 unconfirmed (Enbridge factsheet says 3,090, ~1% off, no source states 3,120 exactly), plus a pre-existing orphan Pressure[ref]. Length (1,131 mi, 2 independent sources) and Owner/Operator (Enbridge, factsheet) sourced at REFS_ADDED; Construction (1953) sourced at low tier with caveats.
